app.name: DTHCMS
app.fullName: Digital Diabetes, Thyroid & Hormone Clinic Management System

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.description: Who signed in, who was given which role, who reset what, who broke the glass — every entry as a sentence, and the chain that proves none is missing.
audit.offline: The clinic server cannot be reached.
audit.unexpected: That did not complete. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the developer.

filters.title: Narrow the trail
filters.personHint: Employee code, as actor or subject.
filters.patientHint: Patient id, for entries about one record.

chain.okTitle: {count, plural, =0 {The chain is empty} one {# entry, chain intact} other {# entries, chain intact}}
chain.okBody: Every hash recomputed and every link checked, up to entry #{head}. This check is now itself in the trail.
chain.strays: {count, plural, one {# entry has} other {# entries have}} landed in the safety-net partition: the monthly partitions need creating. Tell the developer.
chain.brokenTitle: The chain is broken at entry #{seq}

export.done: Saved {file} and its signature (key {key}). Keep the two files together; either alone proves nothing.

kind.priceReview: The month’s medicine prices need checking

breakGlass.title: Emergency access
breakGlass.description: For the record your role does not reach and the patient who cannot wait.
breakGlass.offline: The clinic server cannot be reached. Nothing was opened.
breakGlass.unexpected: That did not complete. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the developer.
breakGlass.opened: Emergency access is open until {until}. Every administrator has been told.

warning.title: Before you open this
warning.body: Your reason is kept word for word. Every administrator is alerted at once, the access is written into the audit chain, and everything you read under it is attributed to you. Use it for the patient in front of you, not for convenience.

form.title: Open access
form.patientHint: The record's id, from the wristband or the registration desk.
form.otherHint: Name it so an administrator can tell what was reached.
form.justificationRemaining: {count, plural, one {# more character needed} other {# more characters needed}} — at least twenty, typed.
form.justificationHint: Kept with the record and shown to the administrators.

connection.offlineDetail: You are offline. Nothing you enter here will be lost, but it will not reach the clinic record until the connection returns.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: The clinic's tablets and phones: which may record values, and what each one is.
devices.offline: The clinic server cannot be reached. Nothing was changed.
devices.unexpected: That did not complete. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the administrator.

register.title: Register a device
register.body: Give the device a name the clinic will recognise. You will get a code to type into it; the code works for fifteen minutes.
register.name: Name
register.nameHint: For example “Anthropometry tablet 2”. Unique within the clinic.
register.nameTaken: A device with that name already exists.

code.title: Enrolment code for {name}
code.body: On the device, open Sign in → Device and type this code. It stops working at {time}.
code.label: Enrolment code
code.onceBody: When you close this panel the code is gone. If it is lost or expires, issue a new one from the list; the old one stops working.

list.title: Enrolled devices
list.empty: No devices yet. Register the first tablet above.
list.name: Device

confirm.reasonHint: Recorded against the device, for whoever reads its history later.

suspend.title: Suspend {name}?
suspend.body: It will be refused until it is reinstated. Anyone signed in on it is signed out on their next request.

reinstate.title: Reinstate {name}?
reinstate.body: It will be accepted again from its next request.

revoke.title: Revoke {name}?
revoke.body: This cannot be undone. Its key is retired and every session on it is ended. To use the hardware again, register it as a new device.

lost.title: Report {name} lost?
lost.body: This cannot be undone. Like a revocation — and anything the device had queued and sends later is held for review rather than accepted.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: This screen could not be shown. Nothing you entered has been discarded.
error.referenceHelp: Quote this reference when reporting the problem.
error.neverReachedServer: This request did not reach the clinic server, so the reference above will not appear in its records.

notFound.title: This page does not exist
notFound.body: The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved.

denied.title: Not available to your role
denied.body: Your account does not have access to this area. If that is wrong, an administrator can change it.

login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: DTHC clinic staff only.
login.offlineTitle: The clinic server cannot be reached
login.offlineBody: Check the network connection and try again. Nothing was sent.
login.unexpected: Sign-in did not complete. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the administrator.

dashboard.title: Dashboard

patients.title: Patients
patients.description: Search, register and open a patient record.

stations.title: Stations
stations.description: Desktop fallback for station work when a tablet is unavailable.

qa.title: Quality control
qa.description: Review of recorded measurements before they reach the clinical record.

followUp.title: Follow-up
followUp.description: Calls, reminders and the patients who have not returned.

research.title: Research
research.description: Anonymised cohorts and the named analyses.

admin.title: Administration
admin.description: Users, roles, devices and clinic configuration.

users.title: Users
users.body: Invite colleagues, grant and revoke roles, suspend accounts, and reset credentials.

devices.title: Devices
devices.body: Register the clinic's tablets and phones, and revoke the ones that leave.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: Read who did what, verify the chain, export a signed PDF.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Clinic performance for the management view.

audit.description: Every security-relevant act, as a sentence, chained.

breakGlass.title: Emergency access
breakGlass.description: Open a record your role does not reach, on the record.

register.title: Register a patient
register.description: Step 1 of the journey: the record everything else hangs from.

board.title: Clinic traffic control
board.description: Where every patient is, and where the floor is backed up.

alerts.title: Critical values
alerts.description: Everything raised in this clinic that nobody has answered yet — least answered first.

counselingTemplates.title: Counselling checklists
counselingTemplates.description: Write and publish the checklist a counsellor works through, without waiting for a release.

corrections.title: Corrections
corrections.description: Values a colleague has asked you to check, and what you decided about them.

myQuality.title: My correction record
myQuality.description: What you recorded, what was questioned, and what happened to it.

qualityTeam.title: Correction patterns
qualityTeam.description: Recurring patterns worth a conversation, with the record each one came from.

jobs.title: Background work
jobs.description: Every registered job type, whether or not anything is queued: how much is waiting, how long it has waited, what has been given up on, and whether the five-minute promise is being kept.

formulary.title: Medicine formulary
formulary.description: What this clinic prescribes, what each medicine costs, and the monthly review of those prices.

medicines.title: Find a medicine
medicines.description: Two letters, and the medicine with its molecule, strength, form and price.

medicationRules.title: Medication safety rules
medicationRules.description: Write, test and publish the rules that check every prescription.

placeholder.title: {area} is not built yet
placeholder.body: This screen exists so the shell can be navigated and reviewed. It lands at {checkpoint}.
placeholder.unscheduled: This area is in the frontend architecture but has no checkpoint scheduled yet.

realtime.liveDetail: This screen is receiving updates as they happen.
realtime.reconnectingDetail: The live connection dropped and is being re-established. The screen will catch up by itself.
realtime.offlineDetail: This screen is not receiving updates and may be behind. Anything you save is still recorded — it is only the automatic refresh that has stopped.

secondFactor.codeHint: The six digits your app shows now.
secondFactor.recoveryHint: One of the codes you saved when you set up the authenticator. It works once.
secondFactor.loginBody: Your password was accepted. Now the code from your authenticator app.
secondFactor.offline: The clinic server cannot be reached.
secondFactor.notEnrolled: This account has no authenticator set up. Set one up under Account → Security.
secondFactor.unexpected: That did not complete. Try again.
secondFactor.nudgeBody: Your role requires a second factor to sign prescriptions, change roles or export data. It takes two minutes.

security.title: Security
security.description: Your authenticator app, and the recovery codes for the day you do not have it.
security.offline: The clinic server cannot be reached. Nothing was changed.
security.unexpected: That did not complete. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the administrator.
security.wrongCode: The code did not match. Check the time on your phone and try the next one.
security.disabled: The authenticator has been turned off for this account.
security.regenerateStepUp: Replace your recovery codes. The current ones will stop working.
security.disableStepUp: Turn off the authenticator for this account.

factor.title: Authenticator app
factor.onBody: Signing in asks for a six-digit code from your app. Signing a prescription, changing a role, exporting research data and turning this off ask for a fresh one.
factor.offBody: An authenticator app adds a code to your sign-in that only your phone can produce. It works with no network and no SMS.
factor.requiredBody: Physicians, administrators, pharmacists and researchers sign in with a code from an authenticator app. Until yours is set up, nothing that needs one can be done from this account.
factor.codesLeft: {count, plural, =0 {No recovery codes left} one {# recovery code left} other {# recovery codes left}}.
factor.fewCodesTitle: You are nearly out of recovery codes
factor.fewCodesBody: Replace them before you need one.

enrol.title: Set up your authenticator
enrol.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
enrol.step1: Open an authenticator app on your phone — Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis or any app that supports TOTP.
enrol.step2: Scan this code, or enter the key by hand.
enrol.step3: Type the six-digit code the app shows.
enrol.manualSummary: Cannot scan? Enter the key by hand
enrol.manualHint: In the app choose “enter a key manually”, name it DTHCMS, and type:

codes.titleEnrolled: Authenticator on — save these recovery codes
codes.onceBody: Each code signs you in once if your phone is lost. Write them down or print them and keep them somewhere that is not your phone. You will not be able to see them again.

session.expired: Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.

shell.patientsWaiting: {count, plural, =0 {No patients waiting} one {# patient waiting} other {# patients waiting}}

systemStatus.title: Clinic server
systemStatus.description: The only part of the backend this shell talks to. Everything else arrives at CP12.
systemStatus.unreachableDetail: The application cannot reach the clinic server. Check that it is running.

users.title: Users
users.description: Everyone with an account at this clinic: who they are, what they may do, and whether they can sign in.
users.offline: The clinic server cannot be reached. Nothing was changed.
users.unexpected: That did not complete. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the developer.

list.title: People
list.empty: Nobody yet. Invite the first colleague.
list.noMatch: Nobody matches. Clear the search or choose another status.

invite.title: Invite a colleague
invite.body: Create the account here, at the desk. The employee code and first password are shown once when the account exists; read them to the colleague and keep no copy.
invite.checkFields: Some details were not accepted. Check the fields marked below.
invite.codeHint: Capitals, digits and underscores; two to sixteen characters. Unique within the clinic.
invite.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. Read it to the colleague; it is not sent anywhere.

created.title: {name} has an account
created.body: Hand over these two things. The roles you chose decide what the colleague sees; the password is theirs until an administrator sets another.
created.onceBody: When you close this panel the password is gone. If it is lost, set a new one from the account page.

roles.title: Roles
roles.label: Roles
roles.previewTitle: {count, plural, =0 {No permissions yet} one {# permission in effect} other {# permissions in effect}}
roles.previewEmpty: Tick a role to see what it lets the person do.
roles.previewAdded: {count, plural, one {# would be added} other {# would be added}} — shown outlined.
roles.none: No roles yet. Until one is granted this person can sign in but do nothing.
roles.effective: {count, plural, =0 {No permissions in effect} one {# permission in effect} other {# permissions in effect}}

revoke.title: Revoke {role} from {name}?
revoke.body: The role stops applying at once, on every device. The grant stays in the history with your reason.

grant.button: {count, plural, =0 {Grant roles} one {Grant # role} other {Grant # roles}}

account.title: Account
account.selfLocked: Your own account's status is changed by another administrator, not by you.

active.title: Activate {name}?
active.body: The person can sign in again with the roles they hold.

suspended.title: Suspend {name}?
suspended.body: Sign-in is refused and every open session ends. Nothing is deleted; a suspended account can be reactivated.

deactivated.title: Deactivate {name}?
deactivated.body: For someone who has left. Sign-in is refused, every session ends, and their history stays. The account can be reactivated if they return.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.recoveryCodes: {count, plural, =0 {No recovery codes left} one {# recovery code left} other {# recovery codes left}}

authenticator.label: Authenticator
authenticator.title: Reset {name}'s authenticator?
authenticator.body: For a colleague who has lost the phone and the recovery codes. The old seed stops working, every session ends, and the next sign-in asks them to set up a new authenticator.
authenticator.done: {name}'s authenticator was reset. They set up a new one at the next sign-in.

password.label: New password
password.hint: At least {min} characters. Read it to the colleague; it is shown nowhere else.
password.title: Set a new password for {name}
password.body: Every open session ends. The colleague signs in with this password from now on.
password.done: {name}'s password was set. Their sessions were ended.

sessions.label: Signed in on
sessions.title: Sign {name} out everywhere?
sessions.body: {count, plural, one {The open session ends} other {All # open sessions end}} at once. The person can sign in again immediately.
sessions.done: {name}: {count, plural, =0 {no sessions were open} one {# session was ended} other {# sessions were ended}}.

history.title: Role history
history.empty: No role has been granted yet.

confirm.reasonRequired: Kept with the record. At least three characters.
confirm.reasonOptional: Optional, but kept with the record if given.

verify.title: Prescription verification
verify.subtitle: Check that a printed prescription came from DTHC.
verify.placeholderNotice: Verification is not built yet. This page is public by design — a patient scanning the code on a printed prescription has no account — and it lands at CP95.
verify.publicNotice: This page is public. It shows only whether a prescription is genuine, never its contents.

duplicates.blockedBody: The record below already holds this identity number, or this mobile with this exact date of birth. Open it rather than creating a second one.
duplicates.reviewBody: {count, plural, one {One existing record looks similar. Check it before continuing.} other {# existing records look similar. Check them before continuing.}}
duplicates.differentHint: Common in this register — many people share a name and a birth year. Say so and carry on.

merge.title: Are these the same person?
merge.lede: Read both columns. Merging joins two clinical histories into one and cannot be undone.
merge.compareCaption: The two records side by side. Differences are marked.
merge.differentHint: No reason needed. Nothing is changed.
merge.survivorLine: {merged} will redirect to {survivor}. Nothing is deleted.
merge.justification: Why do you believe these are the same person?
merge.justificationPlaceholder: Same person: second registration at the outreach camp on 12 August, NID card was at home.
merge.justificationHint: At least {min} characters. Somebody may read this in a year and need to understand the decision.
merge.irreversible: You will be asked for your authenticator code. The merge cannot be undone.
merge.failed: The merge could not be completed.

review.title: Possible duplicate records
review.description: Records that may be the same person. Nothing is merged unless you decide it.
review.lede: Compared against {clinicalId}. Open one to see the two records side by side.
review.noneBody: Nobody else in this clinic's register looks like this person.
review.loadFailed: That record could not be loaded.
review.mergedBody: Everything now lives under {clinicalId}. Nothing was deleted.

register.title: Register a patient
register.description: The clinical minimum is enough to finish. Everything below it is prompted and skippable.

sections.identityNote: The English name and the date of birth are what everything else hangs from.
sections.identifiersNote: The number is hashed and sealed before it is stored. Screens show only the last four digits.
sections.socioNote: Used for research cohorts. Leave anything blank that was not asked — that is different from “unknown”, which means asked and not known.
sections.consentNote: A patient cannot be registered without a recorded consent.

register.phoneHelp: 01712345678 — any format; it is stored one way.
register.phoneSecondaryHelp: A landline or an overseas number.
register.consentHelp: The reference of the consent taken at the desk.
register.failed: The registration could not be saved.
register.blocked: This person is already registered. Open the record above instead of creating a second one.

missing.birthDate: the date of birth and where it came from

register.nextStation: Send the patient to Anthropometry with this number.

birth.hint: The year alone is enough if that is all they know.
birth.ageApproximate: About {years} years old — the exact date is not known
birth.unreadable: That is not a date. Check the day and month.
birth.future: That date has not happened yet.
birth.implausible: That would make them over 130. Check the year.
birth.sourceHelp: A researcher needs to tell a document from a recollection.
birth.documentIsExact: A document carries an exact date. Enter the day, or say the date was stated rather than seen.

photo.title: Patient photograph
photo.note: Resized in the browser and uploaded straight to storage. It is never public and the link expires.
photo.tooLarge: That file is too large. Take the photograph with the camera rather than choosing a large one.
photo.uploadFailed: The photograph could not be uploaded. Try again.

correct.pageDescription: Nothing is overwritten. Every change is recorded with what it was, what it is now, and why.
correct.title: Correct demographics
correct.lede: Editing {clinicalId}. Change only the fields that are wrong — anything you leave alone is not sent.
correct.highImpactTitle: This correction affects values already computed
correct.highImpactBody: The date of birth, its precision, the sex and the English name are used to derive percentiles, reference ranges and research cohorts. You will be asked for your authenticator code.
correct.reasonPlaceholder: The NID card reads 1985; the desk typed 1958.
correct.reasonHint: At least {min} characters. “Correction” is not a reason — say what the right value came from.
correct.willChange: {count, plural, one {# field will change} other {# fields will change}}.
correct.failed: That correction could not be recorded. Nothing has changed.
correct.neverOverwritten: The previous value stays in the record permanently and remains visible below.
correct.doneBody: {count, plural, one {# field was changed} other {# fields were changed}}. The previous values remain in the record.
correct.loadFailed: That record could not be loaded.

history.caption: {count, plural, one {# recorded change} other {# recorded changes}}, newest first.
history.failed: The correction history could not be loaded.
history.none: This record has never been corrected.
history.note: Previous values are kept permanently. Nothing in this table can be edited or removed.

consent.pageDescription: What this patient has agreed to. Each is separate, and each can be withdrawn at any time.
consent.title: Consent
consent.lede: Five separate permissions. Agreeing to treatment is not agreeing to a text message.
consent.noWordingTitle: The approved wording is not loaded yet
consent.noWordingBody: The consent text is a legal document and is still with counsel. Consent cannot be recorded until it is published — a consent taken against no words is a consent to nothing in particular.
consent.versionLine: Version {version}, {language}. This exact text is recorded with the consent.
consent.versionNote: The version, the language and a digest of the text above are stored with the consent, so what was shown can be produced years later.
consent.witnessHint: Required for a thumbprint or a verbal consent — the only other person present is you.
consent.paperHint: The number on the form, so it can be found again.
consent.recordFailed: That consent could not be recorded. Nothing has changed.
consent.uploadFailed: The signature could not be uploaded. Try again.
consent.padHint: Sign or press a thumb in the box.
consent.withdrawBody: This takes effect immediately. The original consent stays in the record with the date it was given.
consent.withdrawReasonHint: Optional. A patient does not have to explain.

explain.care: Examination, tests and treatment at this clinic.
explain.communication: Appointment reminders and results by telephone or SMS.
explain.research: An anonymised row in studies. No name, no number, no address.
explain.ai_processing: The record may be read by an AI assistant to help the physician.
explain.outreach: Home visits and invitations to community camps.

board.title: Clinic traffic
board.reasonPlaceholder: Examination is backed up; nutrition is free
board.moved: That patient has already moved on. The board has been refreshed.
board.rerouteFailed: The move could not be recorded. Nothing has changed.
board.unavailable: The board cannot be read right now.

empty.title: Nobody is waiting
empty.body: Patients appear here as soon as they join a station's queue.

observations.title: Values
observations.shapeNotShown: This kind of value cannot be shown on this screen.

growth.lede: Height, weight and BMI against the reference for this child’s exact age.
growth.title: Growth percentiles
growth.caption: Reference: {standards}. The dashed line is the 95th percentile.

note.no_reference_for_sex: No published growth reference covers this patient’s recorded sex.
note.too_old_for_a_growth_reference: Growth percentiles apply up to 20 years of age.
note.nothing_measured_yet: No height, weight or BMI has been recorded yet.

alerts.title: Critical value alerts
alerts.unavailable: Critical values cannot be read right now.
alerts.unavailableBody: This screen cannot see whether anything is waiting. Ask the desk, and tell the developer if it does not come back.

empty.title: Nothing is waiting
empty.body: Every critical value raised in this clinic has been acknowledged. A new one appears here within seconds of being raised.

alerts.raisedAgo: {minutes, plural, =0 {raised just now} other {raised # min ago}}
alerts.escalatedTo: Nobody answered. This has gone to escalation step {step, number}.
alerts.notDelivered: This reached no screen. Nobody has been told — go and find somebody.
alerts.note: What you are doing about it
alerts.noteDescription: The next person to open this record reads this instead of asking you. “Giving oral glucose, rechecking in 15” — not “seen”.
alerts.notePlaceholder: Giving oral glucose, rechecking in 15 minutes
alerts.acknowledgeFailedBody: Nothing has changed and the escalation is still running. Try again, or go and find somebody.
alerts.alreadyTakenUnknown: Another clinician acknowledged this one while you were writing.
alerts.stripCount: {count, plural, one {# critical value nobody has answered} other {# critical values nobody has answered}}
alerts.patientUnavailable: This patient’s critical values could not be read. Do not read this screen as an all-clear.
alerts.valueHistory: See every value recorded for this measurement

terminology.label: Diagnosis or finding
terminology.description: The clinic’s own list is here before you type. After that, three letters of the name — or the code itself.
terminology.resultCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing matched} one {# code found} other {# codes found}}

reason.word: A word in the name starts with what you typed
reason.spelling: Close to the spelling you typed

empty.title: Nothing matched “{query}”
empty.body: Try fewer letters, or type the code itself — E11.9 finds it when the words will not.
empty.noFavourites: This clinic has no list of its own yet
empty.noFavouritesBody: Nobody has ranked the diagnoses made here. Type three letters of a name, or the code.

terminology.refused: This terminology cannot be searched here.
terminology.unreachable: The code list cannot be reached.
terminology.unreachableBody: Write the diagnosis in your own words instead. It is kept, and somebody can add the code later — do not wait for this list.

history.lede: Complaints, other conditions, family, operations, current medicines and vaccinations — asked in that order, and confirmed rather than assumed.
history.title: Medical history
history.unavailable: This patient’s history could not be read.
history.unavailableBody: Do not read this screen as an empty history. Ask the patient, and tell the developer if it does not come back.
history.noKinds: The kinds of history could not be read, so nothing can be recorded here yet.

empty.title: Nothing has been recorded for this patient
empty.body: Not the same as a patient with nothing wrong. Ask, and record what she brings with her.

lifestyle.title: Smoking and alcohol are not asked here
lifestyle.body: They are recorded at the lifestyle station and shown with this patient’s observations. Asking again would be two answers to one question, with no way to tell which is current.

unconfirmed.title: {count, plural, one {# item nobody has confirmed} other {# items nobody has confirmed}}
unconfirmed.body: Nothing below carries forward on its own. Ask about each one and confirm it yourself — the record names whoever said it is still true, one item at a time.

history.neverConfirmed: Nobody has confirmed this since it was recorded.
history.nothingChanged: Nothing has changed. Try again, or ask somebody.
history.amendNote: Correcting an item also confirms it: you have just said what is true about it now.
history.resolveBody: This keeps the item and records that she had it and no longer does. It stays in the history, which is what makes the next visit read as a follow-up. It is not the same as saying it should never have been recorded.
history.resolveFailed: This item was not marked as resolved.
history.remove: This should not have been recorded
history.removeBody: Use this only when the item is wrong — the wrong patient, a mishearing, a duplicate. Nothing is deleted: the item and your reason both stay in the record. If she had this and no longer does, close this and say so instead.
history.removeReason: Why should this not have been recorded?
history.removeReasonHint: Whoever reads this later needs to know what you disagreed with.
history.removeReasonPlaceholder: Recorded on the wrong patient — this is her sister’s file.
history.recordFailed: The item was not recorded. Nothing has changed.

reconciliation.UNRECONCILED: Not yet matched to the clinic’s medicine list
reconciliation.MATCHED: Matched to the clinic’s medicine list
reconciliation.NOT_STOCKED: This clinic does not stock it

required.said: Say what she described, in her words. An item with no code needs one.
required.relation: Say which relative this is about.
required.duration_days: Say how many days she has had it.

form.kind: What kind of item is this?
form.kindHint: Each kind is coded from its own list and asks for different details.
form.conceptHint: Search the list this kind is coded from. If nothing fits, leave it and write what she said below.
form.saidHint: Her own words, kept beside the code. “Sugar since the flood” is the clinical detail; the code’s title is not.
form.saidRequired: Required, because nothing has been coded. Write what she described so somebody can code it later.
form.saidPlaceholder: Burning in the chest after the evening meal, for about three weeks
form.relationHint: Coded, so a question about first-degree relatives can be asked of the whole register.
form.durationHint: Roughly is fine — three weeks is 21. It is what separates a complaint from a diagnosis.
form.severityHint: Her answer, not yours. Leave it out if she did not say.
form.onsetHint: Leave it out if she does not know.
form.precisionHint: “About two years ago” is a real answer. Say so here, rather than writing a day nobody meant.
form.doseHint: As she takes it, not as it is prescribed.

allergies.lede: The one question a patient cannot go past the history station without an answer to. Three answers satisfy it, and there is no fourth.
allergies.title: Allergies
allergies.unavailable: This patient’s allergy status could not be read.
allergies.unavailableBody: Do not read this as a patient with no allergies. Ask, and tell the developer if it does not come back.
allergies.notPermitted: You may not read this patient’s allergies while wearing this role.
allergies.noReactions: The list of reactions could not be read, so no allergy can be recorded here yet.

status.ALLERGIES_RECORDED: {count, plural, one {# allergy recorded} other {# allergies recorded}}

statusBody.NONE_RECORDED: Nobody has asked yet. This is not the same as a patient with no allergies.
statusBody.ALLERGIES_RECORDED: Worst first: the one that could stop a heart is at the top of this list.
statusBody.NO_KNOWN_ALLERGY: Somebody asked and was told there are none. A statement by a person, not an empty field.
statusBody.UNABLE_TO_ASSESS: Somebody asked and could not get an answer. This does not say the patient has no allergies.

gate.blocked: This patient cannot be sent past the history station.
gate.how: Record an allergy, or state that there are no known allergies, or say why it could not be assessed. Nothing else opens the way, here or anywhere.

empty.title: Nobody has asked about allergies yet
empty.body: This is not a record of no allergies. Until somebody answers, this patient cannot be sent past the history station.

assert.reason: Why could the answer not be got?
assert.reasonHint: Whoever reviews this later needs to know what stopped you asking.
assert.reasonPlaceholder: Patient is drowsy and no attendant is present.

NO_KNOWN_ALLERGY.title: Say that there are no known allergies
NO_KNOWN_ALLERGY.body: This puts a statement in the record with your name on it: you asked, and the patient knows of no allergy. It is not a default and not an empty field — whoever hands over the medicine will rely on it. Ask before you press it.

UNABLE_TO_ASSESS.title: Say that the answer could not be got
UNABLE_TO_ASSESS.body: For the patient who cannot answer and has nobody with them. This is allergy status, not a way past the question: it records that somebody looked, and it never says there are none. The reason is required because somebody will read it.
UNABLE_TO_ASSESS.confirm: Record that it could not be assessed

allergies.assertFailed: Nothing was recorded. The allergy status has not changed.
allergies.recordFailed: The allergy was not recorded. Nothing has changed.
allergies.nothingChanged: Nothing has changed. Try again, or ask somebody.

form.substanceHint: Search the clinic’s own dictionary. If it is not there, leave this and write what she said instead.
form.saidRequired: Required, because nothing has been coded. Write what she described.
form.saidHint: Kept beside the code. “The yellow tablet from the pharmacy near the bridge” is sometimes the only thing that identifies what happened.
form.saidPlaceholder: The yellow tablet from the pharmacy near the bridge
form.reactionHint: From the list, so every screen afterwards can draw it. The emergencies come first.
form.severityHint: Nothing is chosen for you: a severity nobody stated is a claim nobody made.
form.certaintyHint: A suspected reaction thirty years ago and a confirmed anaphylaxis are not the same warning.
form.noteHint: Optional. What happened, when, and who saw it.

required.said: Say what she described, or pick it from the dictionary.

allergies.withdrawBody: Nothing is deleted: the allergy and your reason both stay in the record, because the next clinician needs to know a colleague once believed it. If this is the only allergy on file, withdrawing it closes the way past the history station again.
allergies.withdrawReasonHint: Whoever reads this later needs to know what you disagreed with.
allergies.withdrawReasonPlaceholder: Recorded on the wrong patient — this is her sister’s file.
allergies.withdrawAssertionBody: The statement and your reason both stay in the record. Unless allergies are on file, this leaves the patient with no allergy status at all, which closes the way past the history station again.
allergies.withdrawAssertionPlaceholder: Tapped on the wrong patient at the desk.

changes.title: Everything ever said about this patient’s allergies
changes.none: Nothing has been said about this patient’s allergies yet.
changes.unavailable: The change history could not be read.

counseling.lede: What a counsellor works through with a patient, written by a physician rather than by a software release.
counseling.unavailable: The counselling checklists could not be read.
counseling.unavailableBody: Do not read this as a clinic with no checklists. Try again, and tell the developer if it keeps failing.
counseling.offline: The request did not reach the server.

list.title: Checklists
list.drafts: {count, plural, one {# draft open} other {# drafts open}}

empty.title: No checklist has been written yet
empty.body: Start one. It stays here as a draft until you publish it, and nothing reaches the floor before then.

approval.notApproved: Content not approved by a clinician
approval.notApprovedBody: These items are a proposal, not an approved clinical list. The ones the clinic started with are transcribed from the plan as a launch minimum, and their Bangla and their guidance text were written by the engineer. A clinician has still to sign them off.

new.title: Start a new checklist
new.body: It is created with an empty first draft. Nothing reaches the floor until you publish it.
new.titleENHint: What a counsellor reading English will see in their list.
new.titleBNHint: Asked for now rather than later. Half this clinic counsels in Bangla.
new.codeHint: Upper case and permanent — THYROID, for example. Assignment rules and audit entries name it, so it does not change when the title does.
new.failed: The checklist could not be created.

required.title_en: A name in English is required.
required.title_bn: A name in Bangla is required.

version.heading: Version {version}
version.unavailable: This version could not be read.
version.frozen: This version is finished and cannot be changed.
version.frozenBody: Every completed counselling session keeps the version it was done against. Editing this one would rewrite what counsellors were asked to cover months ago, and nothing afterwards would look wrong. Draft a new version instead.
version.publishedByPerson: A member of the clinic’s staff
version.publishedBySystemBody: No person published this version. It arrived with the migration that set the clinic up, and a name here would be the only place in this system crediting somebody who did not do the thing.
version.noNotes: No note was left with this version.

empty.title: This version has no items yet
empty.body: An empty checklist cannot be published — on a counsellor’s phone it reads as finished the moment it opens.

version.draftNewBody: It starts as a copy of what is live, so fixing one item does not mean retyping the rest. Nothing changes on the floor until you publish it.
version.draftFailed: A new draft could not be opened.

room.unknown: This room ({code}) is not one the system lists. Its items are shown anyway, so none of them is lost.

editor.title: Editing version {version}
editor.notesHint: Read by whoever compares two versions a year from now.
editor.saveFailed: The draft could not be saved.
editor.conflict: This version was published while you were writing.
editor.conflictBody: A published version is finished and cannot be changed. Draft a new version, and what you have written belongs there.
editor.cannotSave: The draft cannot be saved yet.
editor.notReady: Not ready for the floor yet. This does not stop you saving.
editor.guidanceHint: What to actually say. The physician questions the patient afterwards, and two counsellors who covered this differently make that check useless.
editor.roomHint: A counsellor works through one room, then walks the patient to the next.
editor.itemCodeHint: Stable across versions. Rewording an item keeps its history; changing this code does not.
editor.mandatoryHint: A session cannot be closed until every item marked this way is ticked.

blocker.duplicate_code: Item {position} uses the code {code}, which is already taken. Two items with one code make a tick ambiguous.
blocker.no_text: Item {position} has no text in either language.
blocker.unknown_room: Item {position} is in a room the system does not have ({room}).

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: Publishing is not saving. It puts this checklist on every phone on the floor, freezes this version, and retires the one in use.
publish.notReady: This version cannot be published yet.
publish.unsavedBody: Publishing sends the saved version to the floor, not what is on this screen.
publish.failed: The checklist could not be published.
publish.stepUp: Publish version {version} of this counselling checklist

blocker.no_items: There are no items. An empty checklist reads as finished the moment it opens.

confirm.title: Publish version {version}?
confirm.live: Every counsellor’s phone will show this checklist within seconds.
confirm.frozen: Version {version} will be frozen forever. To change anything afterwards you draft a new version.
confirm.retires: Version {version}, which is live now, will be retired.
confirm.nothingRetired: Nothing is live for this checklist yet, so nothing will be retired.
confirm.stepUpNote: You will be asked for a code from your authenticator before this happens.

preview.title: What a counsellor will see
preview.body: The same list, in the order the rooms are walked. Switch the language to check the half you do not work in.

panel.lede: What this patient has been taken through on this visit — each item, who covered it, when, and what is still outstanding.
panel.notPermitted: You do not have permission to read counselling sessions.

visit.label: Visit {code}
visit.closedBody: There is no open visit for this patient, so this is the record of the last one. The checkpoint below describes that visit, not the patient sitting in front of you now.
visit.unavailable: This patient’s visits could not be read.
visit.unavailableBody: Do not read this as a patient nobody has ever counselled. Try again, and tell the developer if it keeps failing.

none.title: This patient has no visit yet
none.body: Counselling is recorded against a visit. Once one is open at registration, the checklists this patient’s conditions call for appear here.

gate.title: The counselling checkpoint
gate.blockedBody: The queue will not take this patient to the next station until the items below are covered — or until somebody with the permission sends them past and says why.
gate.clear: Every mandatory item has been covered
gate.clearBody: Nothing is outstanding on this visit, and nobody has been sent past.
gate.overridden: Sent past the checkpoint with the counselling unfinished
gate.overriddenBody: This patient is not being held, and that is not the same as the checklist being done. Somebody decided to let them through; what was still uncovered at that moment is listed below.
gate.unavailable: The counselling checkpoint could not be read.
gate.unavailableBody: Do not read this as a patient with nothing outstanding. Try again, and tell the developer if it keeps failing.

missing.unfinishedBody: A counsellor opened these checklists and stopped part way. There is a session to go back to; send the patient to the room named beside each item.
missing.notStartedBody: This patient’s conditions call for them and no counsellor has begun. This is a different problem from an unfinished session: there is nothing to return to, and somebody has to start it.
missing.noText: This item has no text in either language.

override.byUnknownRole: By a member of staff whose record could not be read
override.skippedBody: What was still uncovered at that moment, not what is uncovered now. An item covered afterwards does not make the decision retrospectively unnecessary, so it stays on this list.
override.skippedNone: Nothing was recorded as outstanding at that moment.
override.action: Send this patient past the checkpoint
override.title: Send this patient past the counselling checkpoint
override.body: The patient goes on to the next station with the counselling unfinished. This covers nothing: every outstanding item stays outstanding, this visit is recorded as overridden, and your name is on it.
override.reasonLabel: Why this patient is going through without the counselling
override.reasonHint: Read by whoever reviews how often this happens, which is the only thing keeping it from becoming the normal way through. “The interpreter did not arrive” is an answer; a full stop is not.
override.reasonPlaceholder: The insulin corner was closed and the patient’s daughter was waiting with the car.
override.failed: This patient was not sent past the checkpoint.
override.alreadyStands: Somebody has already sent this patient past
override.alreadyStandsBody: Only one override stands on a visit. Reload the screen to see whose it is and what reason they gave.

sessions.title: Checklists walked on this visit
sessions.unavailable: The counselling sessions could not be read.
sessions.unavailableBody: Do not read this as a patient nobody counselled. Try again, and tell the developer if it keeps failing.
sessions.detailUnavailable: The items on this checklist could not be read.
sessions.detailUnavailableBody: The checklist was opened for this patient; what was covered on it cannot be shown at the moment.
sessions.noItems: The version this session walked has no items on it.
sessions.unknownRole: a member of staff whose role was not recorded
sessions.stillOpen: Still open — no counsellor has said they are done.
sessions.outstandingCount: {count, plural, one {# item that must be covered} other {# items that must be covered}}
sessions.allCovered: Nothing — every item that must be covered has been.

empty.title: No checklist has been opened on this visit
empty.body: Either this patient’s record calls for none, or nobody has started one yet. The checkpoint above says which.

item.byUnknownRole: By a member of staff whose record could not be read
item.noText: This item has no text in either language.
item.withdrawnNoReason: No reason was recorded for taking it back.
item.unknownTime: a time that was not recorded
item.undoCount: {count, plural, one {Ticked and taken back once on this session} other {Ticked and taken back # times on this session}}
item.notCoveredOptional: Not covered. This item is optional, so it does not hold the patient.
item.takenBackByUnknown: Taken back by a member of staff whose record could not be read.
item.outstandingHeld: The checkpoint will hold this patient until it is covered.
item.outstandingOverridden: The patient was sent past the checkpoint without it.

time.caveat: Times are the gap between one tick and the next — from the session opening, for the first item. That is what was recorded, and it is not attention: a counsellor who talks through four items and ticks them together at the end shows three fast items and one slow one.
time.unknown: No time can be read for this item.

attribution.heading: Entered by
attribution.byUnknown: A member of staff whose record could not be read
attribution.byNobody: This record does not say who entered the value.
attribution.notListed: This person is not in the staff directory.
attribution.namesUnavailable: The staff directory could not be read, so the name is missing.
attribution.directoryUnavailable: Names could not be read just now. The role, station and time above come from the record itself.

presence.suspended: Not working at the clinic at present.

attribution.deviceUnlisted: Entered on a device that is not in the directory.
attribution.timeUnreadable: The time on this record could not be read.

source.STATION: Typed by an operator at a station.
source.OCR: Read by the scanner from a photograph of paper. Nobody typed it.
source.FIELD: Recorded away from the clinic, on a community visit.
source.DEVICE: Sent by a measuring device, without anybody typing it.
source.PATIENT: Reported by the patient rather than measured here.
source.other: Recorded with a source this screen does not recognise: {source}.
source.unrecorded: The record does not say what kind of evidence this is, and it must not be read as a station entry. Records written before the clinic began storing this are like that.

correction.SUPERSEDED: A later value replaced this one.
correction.AMENDED: A detail of this record was changed later.
correction.byUnrecorded: The record does not name who made the change.
correction.replaced: There is a later value in the record.

flag.title: Ask for {what} to be checked
flag.body: The request goes to the person who recorded this value. The value stays on the record either way — a correction adds a new one beside it.
flag.alreadyOpen: Somebody has already asked about this value
flag.alreadyOpenBody: One request at a time, because a second would send two corrections for one number. The open request is shown above.
flag.nothingChanged: Nothing was sent. The value and the record are unchanged.
flag.failed: The request could not be sent.
flag.reasonsUnavailable: The list of reasons could not be read
flag.reasonsUnavailableBody: A reason has to be one the clinic agreed on, so that repeated problems can be counted. Try again in a moment.
flag.reasonHint: The reason is what the clinic counts. Write what you actually saw in the note below.
flag.counted: Reasons like this one are counted when the clinic looks for repeated typing errors.
flag.notePlaceholder: The tape was against the wall, not the patient
flag.noteHint: Read by the person being asked to correct it. A reason code cannot say this.
flag.confirm: Send to the person who recorded it
flag.yourOwn: This is your own value. Correct it where it was recorded rather than asking somebody else to.

person.unknown: A member of staff whose record could not be read
person.namesUnavailable: The staff directory could not be read, so the name is missing.
person.notListed: This person is not in the staff directory.

presence.suspended: Not working at the clinic at present.

status.APPLIED: Corrected by the person who recorded it

state.CORRECTED: Corrected — the value below replaced it

trail.waiting: Waiting for them to answer. The value on the record has not changed.
trail.overridden: Somebody other than the person who recorded the value corrected it. The record says so, rather than reading as their own correction.
trail.answerNote: Note from the person who corrected it
trail.timeUnreadable: the time on this record could not be read
trail.timeUnknown: the record does not give a time

chain.title: History of {what}
chain.bothKept: The record holds {count, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}} of this measurement. Every one of them is kept; nothing was overwritten.
chain.unavailable: The value history could not be read
chain.unavailableBody: The record is not missing; this screen could not read it. Try again in a moment.
chain.noneBody: No value has been measured under this code, so there is nothing to show.
chain.correctionsUnavailable: The correction requests could not be read
chain.correctionsUnavailableBody: The values below are the record and are shown in full. What is missing is who asked about them and why.

derived.title: What was computed from this
derived.body: A value computed from {what} is worked out again when it is corrected, and the earlier answer is kept beside it.
derived.none: Nothing in this patient's record was computed from {what}.
derived.unavailable: The computed values could not be read
derived.unavailableBody: This screen cannot say whether anything was worked out again. That is not the same as nothing having been.
derived.moved: Computed from the {what} that stands now.
derived.stale: Computed from an earlier {what} rather than the one that stands now, and not worked out again since.
derived.unknownInput: The record does not say which {what} this was computed from.
derived.previousKept: The earlier answer is kept, replaced rather than overwritten.

history.lede: Every value recorded for one measurement, the replaced ones included, with who entered each and who asked about it.
history.codeHint: Only the measurements this patient has a value for.
history.noValues: No values recorded for this patient
history.noValuesBody: Nothing has been measured yet, so there is no history to show.
history.unavailable: This patient's values could not be read
history.unavailableBody: Without them there is no list of measurements to choose from. Try again in a moment.

answer.title: Answer this request
answer.supervisorTitle: This is not your own value
answer.supervisorBody: You may answer it because you hold the supervisor's permission. It will be recorded as your correction and not as theirs — an operator's record must not read as though they had put it right themselves.
answer.alreadyAnsweredBody: Nothing was changed by this attempt. What they decided is shown above.
answer.notYours: This request is somebody else's to answer
answer.notYoursBody: It was sent to the person who recorded the value. Ask them, or somebody who may answer in their place.
answer.nothingChanged: Nothing was changed. The value and the request are as they were.
answer.failed: The answer could not be saved.
answer.valueUnavailable: The value could not be read
answer.valueUnavailableBody: Answering without seeing what was recorded is answering from memory, so nothing is offered here. Try again in a moment.
answer.correctBody: What you type replaces the value above. That value stays on the record, with your name beside the new one.
answer.notCorrectable: This kind of value cannot be corrected from this screen. It has to be corrected where it was recorded.
answer.standsBody: Say why. The person who asked reads this, and an answer with no reason teaches them nothing.
answer.valueLabel: The value as it should read
answer.valueHint: As you measured it, in the unit you measured it in.
answer.unitHint: The unit it was entered in. Change it only if that was the mistake.
answer.noteLabel: What you want the person who asked to know
answer.noteHint: Read by them. It is not counted anywhere.
answer.keepsOriginal: The value above is neither deleted nor altered. Everything computed from it is worked out again, and those earlier answers are kept too.
answer.reasonHint: Required. It is the only thing the person who asked will learn from this.
answer.reasonPlaceholder: Measured twice on the stadiometer; 150 is right

queue.unavailable: Your list could not be read
queue.unavailableBody: An empty screen here is not the same as nothing waiting. Try again in a moment.
queue.emptyAll: Nothing has been asked of you
queue.emptyBody: When a colleague asks about a value you recorded, it appears here.
queue.openChain: See every value recorded for this measurement

window.label: Period
window.refused: The window on this screen and the one the server accepts have gone out of step. Nothing is wrong with your record; pick a period again.

rate.outOf: {corrections, plural, one {# correction} other {# corrections}} out of {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} recorded
rate.perHundred: That is {rate, number} for every 100 entries.
rate.tooFew: Too few entries in this period for a rate to mean anything yet.
rate.moreNeeded: {needed, plural, one {# more entry} other {# more entries}} in this period and a rate will appear.
rate.floorNote: The clinic works out a rate only once there is enough work in the period to draw a line through. Below that it shows none rather than a misleading one.

outcome.upheld: {part, plural, one {# of {whole, number} was corrected by the person who recorded it.} other {# of {whole, number} were corrected by the person who recorded them.}}
outcome.rejected: {part, plural, one {# of {whole, number} was answered by saying the recorded value stands — and it stood.} other {# of {whole, number} were answered by saying the recorded value stands — and they stood.}}
outcome.open: {part, plural, one {# of {whole, number} is still waiting for an answer.} other {# of {whole, number} are still waiting for an answer.}}
outcome.stoodNote: A value that stood means somebody checked and was right. It is kept beside the rest and counted against nobody.
outcome.noneTitle: Nobody asked about anything in this period.
outcome.noneBody: {entries, plural, one {# entry recorded} other {# entries recorded}}, and no correction requested on any of them.
outcome.overridden: {part, plural, one {# of {whole, number} was corrected by a supervisor instead.} other {# of {whole, number} were corrected by a supervisor instead.}}

breakdown.title: Where the corrections were
breakdown.body: The same corrections read three ways. A pattern is something to act on; a single number is not.
breakdown.byCodeHint: Each against how many of that measurement were taken. The same measurement going wrong again and again is usually the instrument rather than the person.
breakdown.byHourHint: The hour the value was recorded, on the clinic’s clock, against how much was recorded in that hour. Somebody who works the late shift records late; the denominator is what keeps that from reading as a pattern.
breakdown.counted: Counted when the clinic looks for repeated typing
breakdown.byReasonHint: Out of the corrections in this period — a reason is a slice of them, not of the entries.

flags.title: Patterns on this record
flags.noneBodyMine: Nothing on your record has crossed one of the clinic’s thresholds. If something does, it appears here at the same moment your supervisor sees it — and it stays here with the answer once somebody has answered it.
flags.noneBody: Nothing on this record has crossed one of the clinic’s thresholds.
flags.queueTitle: Patterns waiting to be looked at
flags.unavailable: The patterns could not be read
flags.unavailableBody: An empty screen here does not mean nothing is waiting. Try again in a moment.
flags.queueEmptyTitle: Nothing is waiting to be looked at.
flags.queueEmptyBody: No pattern has crossed a threshold and gone unanswered.
flags.queueEmptyAllBody: Nothing has been raised in this clinic at all.
flags.allProposalsTitle: None of these thresholds has been approved yet
flags.allProposalsBody: Every number behind the rows below is a proposal waiting for a clinician to agree to it. They show that the mechanism works; they are not clinic policy, and nobody should be asked to answer for one as though they were.
flags.answeredStay: Answered patterns stay here for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} with what was decided and by whom, rather than disappearing when somebody closes them.

flag.unapprovedTitle: These numbers have not been approved
flag.unapprovedBody: The threshold this was raised on is a proposal no clinician has agreed to yet. Read it as a question, not as a finding.
flag.noEvidence: The supporting corrections could not be read from this row. Do not act on it until they can.
flag.wasDismissed: Answered: this is not a problem
flag.statusAsOf: The outcomes above are as they stood on {when}, frozen with the rest of this row. Open the correction itself for what has happened since.

answer.acknowledgeBody: Says you have read it and are doing something about it. Nothing is removed, and what you write is kept with your name against it.
answer.noteLabel: What you are doing about it
answer.noteHint: Optional here, and read by whoever looks at this record next.
answer.acknowledgeConfirm: Record that I have seen it
answer.dismissBody: Says the pattern is not worth acting on. Frequently the right answer — the instrument, the rota, or a threshold nobody has approved.
answer.reasonLabel: Why it is not a problem
answer.reasonHint: Required. A dismissal with no reason teaches nobody anything, and it is the only thing that takes a pattern off a colleague’s record.
answer.reasonPlaceholder: The scale at station two was reading three kilos light all fortnight.
answer.dismissConfirm: Record that it is not a problem
answer.alreadyAnsweredBody: A colleague got there first. What they decided is on the row now.
answer.failed: The answer could not be sent.
answer.nothingChanged: Nothing was recorded. The pattern is still waiting.

mine.lead: Everything you recorded in this period, what came back, and what happened to it. It is here so that you see it first, not so that anybody keeps a file.
mine.unavailable: Your record could not be read
mine.unavailableBody: Nothing is being kept from you; this screen could not read it. Try again in a moment.

team.lead: The patterns worth a conversation, and the record each one came from. Two of the three suggested first steps point at the instrument and the rota rather than at a person, which is usually where the answer is.

operators.title: Everybody who recorded something
operators.openFlags: {count, plural, one {# pattern waiting to be looked at} other {# patterns waiting to be looked at}}
operators.unavailable: The list could not be read
operators.unavailableBody: An empty list here does not mean nobody was asked about anything. Try again in a moment.
operators.noneTitle: Nobody recorded anything in this period.
operators.noneBody: That is the ordinary state of a closed fortnight, not a sign that anything failed.
operators.recordUnavailable: This record could not be read
operators.recordUnavailableBody: Nothing was changed. Try again in a moment.
operators.roster: Everybody who recorded anything in this period, including the people nothing came back on. They are here on purpose: a list every row of which has a correction on it is an accusation however it is titled.
operators.narrowed: Narrowed to the people who received at least one correction. Absence from this shorter list means only that nothing came back on their work.

thresholds.title: What would raise a pattern
thresholds.body: The three shapes the clinic looks for, and what it suggests doing about each. Readable by everybody, because a rule you are measured against and cannot read is a rule you will assume is worse than it is.
thresholds.proposal: A proposal. No clinician has approved these numbers.
thresholds.allProposalsBody: The numbers are rows a clinician can change rather than something built into the software, and none of them has been approved yet.
thresholds.unavailable: The rules could not be read
thresholds.unavailableBody: The numbers above still stand; what is missing is the explanation of what would raise a pattern.

age.seconds: {count, plural, =0 {just now} one {# second} other {# seconds}}

health.title: Queue health
health.unavailable: The queue’s health could not be read
health.unavailableBody: Nothing on this page is current. A queue that cannot be read looks exactly like a queue with nothing in it, so read this as unknown rather than as quiet. If it keeps happening, look at the server before assuming the work is being done.
health.overWindow: Failure and deadline figures cover the last {window}. Depth, age and what is running are as of now.
health.asOf: Read at {at}, and again every fifteen seconds.
health.needAttention: {part, number} of {whole, number} job types need a look.
health.allWell: Nothing needs a look across all {whole, number} job types.
health.noKindsBody: The catalogue is empty, which is not a quiet morning: it means nothing can be put on the queue at all. This is a deployment to look at rather than a queue.

window.label: How far back the rates look

jobs.pausedNote: Stopped on purpose. Nothing of this type is being taken, and what is already queued stays queued until somebody resumes it.
jobs.waitingCount: {count, plural, one {# job waiting} other {# jobs waiting}}
jobs.confirmResume: Let this type be taken again?

conflict.JOB_NOT_RETRYABLE: Somebody has already retried this one.
conflict.JOB_NOT_CANCELLABLE: A worker has picked this one up, so it can no longer be cancelled.
conflict.JOB_KIND_ALREADY_PAUSED: Somebody has already paused this job type.
conflict.JOB_KIND_NOT_PAUSED: Somebody has already resumed this job type.
conflict.body: Nothing went wrong and nothing needs doing again: the screen was showing a moment that had passed. It has been read afresh, so what is below is current.

jobs.controlFailedBody: The server did not answer, so nothing has changed. The page has been read again — check the state below before trying a second time.

deadLetters.title: Given up on
deadLetters.lead: Jobs that used up every attempt their retry policy allows. This list is not limited by the window above: whenever they failed, they are all here.
deadLetters.emptyTitle: Nothing has been given up on
deadLetters.emptyBody: No job has used up its attempts. A row in the table above can still be stuck or paused, so read that first if something you expected has not happened.

queued.title: Waiting
queued.lead: Jobs no worker has taken yet. A job sitting out the wait between two attempts counts as waiting too, which is why the attempt number is on every row.
queued.emptyBody: Everything put on the queue for this type has been taken.

list.unavailable: This list could not be read
list.unavailableBody: An empty list and an unreadable one look the same, and one of them means work is sitting here that nobody has been asked to look at.
list.capped: The newest {count, number} are shown. There may be more behind them.

detail.unavailable: This job could not be read
detail.unavailableBody: It may have been tidied away, or the server did not answer. Go back to the list and read it again.

fact.dedupe: Key that stops it being queued twice

jobs.argsTitle: What it was asked to do
jobs.argsHint: References only — ids, codes and counts. A job may point at a patient’s record and may never carry anything out of it; the database refuses that on the way in and re-checks the whole table afterwards.

attempts.title: Attempts, and what each one said
attempts.none: No attempt has failed. Either it has not run yet, or it ran cleanly.
attempts.truncated: Each error is shortened to fit. The whole of it is in the log, under this job’s id.

jobs.cancelReasonHint: Required. A cancelled job that says nothing is a gap somebody has to explain later, and you are the person who can explain it now.

done.retriedBody: The attempt count was reset, so the retry policy applies again from the start.
done.cancelledBody: It will not be picked up. The reason you gave is kept with it.

jobs.noneDue: none of it due yet — waiting between attempts
jobs.deadLetterCount: {count, plural, one {# job is waiting for somebody} other {# jobs are waiting for somebody}}

running.title: Running now
running.lead: Jobs a worker has claimed and is working on. One that has been running far longer than the others usually means a wedged worker rather than a hard job — the lease holder on each row says which process has it.
running.emptyBody: No worker is holding a job of this type at this moment.

missed.title: Missed their deadline
missed.lead: Jobs that finished after the deadline their type carries. They succeeded, so they are not among the ones given up on, and they are finished, so they are not waiting — this is the only place they appear. The percentage above is what these rows add up to.
missed.emptyBody: Every finished job that carried a deadline met it.

jobs.seeMissed: {count, plural, one {See the one that missed} other {See the # that missed}}
jobs.seeMissedNamed: See the jobs of type {kind} that missed their deadline

dashboard.title: Patient dashboard
dashboard.description: Open a patient to see the snapshot, the clinical summary and the AI assistant on one screen.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.note: Shortcuts do not fire while you are typing in a field.

breakGlass.title: You are reading this record under emergency access
breakGlass.body: Your reason: “{justification}”. Every administrator was told when you opened it.
breakGlass.notAcknowledged: No administrator has seen it yet

refused.title: This record is not open to you
refused.body: Nothing is said about whether this patient exists. If the situation is an emergency, you can open the record with a typed justification that every administrator sees immediately.

missing.title: No such patient here
missing.body: This facility has no patient with that identifier.

failed.title: The dashboard could not be read
failed.body: Nothing has been hidden. Try again, and use the register if this continues.

snapshot.title: Patient snapshot
snapshot.alerts: {count, plural, one {# unanswered critical value} other {# unanswered critical values}}
snapshot.noVitals: Nothing has been measured for this patient yet.
snapshot.noConditions: Nothing coded. That is not the same as nothing wrong — an uncoded complaint has no row here.
snapshot.counselingBlocked: {count, plural, one {# item not covered} other {# items not covered}}
snapshot.counselingOverridden: Sent past the checkpoint — counselling was not completed

trend.change: {delta} over {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

gap.no_hba1c_in_12_months: No HbA1c in the last twelve months.
gap.station_not_reached: A station on this visit was not reached.
gap.no_history_recorded: No medical history has been recorded for this patient.
gap.no_allergy_status: Nobody has recorded an allergy status.
gap.no_blood_pressure: No blood pressure has been recorded on this visit.

ai.title: Written by AI
ai.caution: A draft. Check every line against the record before acting on it. · এআই-নির্মিত খসড়া। কাজ করার আগে প্রতিটি লাইন রেকর্ডের সঙ্গে মিলিয়ে দেখুন।

summary.title: Clinical summary
summary.noVisit: This patient has not been seen yet, so there is nothing to summarise.
summary.readTheRecord: There is no narrative to read. The structured record is in the panel beside this one, and every value in it names who entered it.
summary.requestFailed: The request could not be sent. The record beside this is unaffected.

grounding.PASSED: Every claim traced to the record
grounding.FAILED: A claim could not be traced — the summary was withheld

provenance.confidenceValue: {value}% — the model's opinion of itself, not a probability about the patient

assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.noVisit: This patient has not been seen yet, so there is nothing to suggest.
assistant.nothingYet: Nothing has been suggested for this visit.
assistant.fromRecordNote: Computed from what is stored. No model was involved in these.
assistant.visitClosed: This visit is closed, so its drafts can no longer be answered.
assistant.notAPrescription: Accepting records that you agree with this draft. It does not write a prescription.
assistant.decidedAgainstOlderRun: You decided this against generation {generation}, and the summary has been prepared again since.
assistant.decideFailed: That could not be recorded. Nothing has changed.
assistant.staleError: The summary has been prepared again. Reload the page and decide on the current suggestions.

basis.open: {count, plural, one {# supporting fact} other {# supporting facts}}

picker.title: Registered today
picker.lede: Patients registered at the desk today. Somebody who registered earlier and is here this morning is in the register, not in this list.
picker.noneBody: Find the patient in the register.
picker.failed: Today's registrations could not be read
picker.failedBody: Nothing has been hidden. The register still works.

timeline.lede: The whole record on one time axis. Drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, and move across the chart to read any value and who recorded it.
timeline.chartLabel: Patient timeline. Use the left and right arrow keys to move across the values.
timeline.altText: {lanes} event lanes and {series} value series, from {from} to {to}. Move the pointer across the chart, or press the left and right arrow keys, to read a value and who recorded it.
timeline.failed: The timeline could not be read just now.
timeline.emptyRecord: Nothing is on this patient's record yet.
timeline.noLanes: Every lane is turned off. Turn one back on to see events.
timeline.hint: Scroll or pinch to zoom. Hover a bar or a value to see who recorded it.

flag.corrected: Corrected — this is not the value that stands today

filter.searchHelp: Brand name, generic name or manufacturer.

list.title: The formulary
list.emptyBody: Try a shorter search, or clear the class filter.
list.emptyUnverified: Every price in this list has been checked by somebody. Nothing is waiting for the review.

asOf.label: What did this cost on…
asOf.hint: Pick a date to see the price that was in force then — not today's price.
asOf.none: This clinic had not priced this medicine on {day}.

record.title: Record a new price
record.explain: The old price is not changed. It is closed on the day the new one starts, and stays in the history.
record.amountHelp: In taka, like 12.50. At most two decimal places.
record.fromHelp: Today, unless you are recording a change you learned about late.
record.confirm: This is what this clinic charges
record.confirmHelp: Leave this off to record what a supplier's list says without confirming it.

history.title: Price history
history.emptyBody: Nobody has recorded what this clinic charges for this medicine.

review.title: Monthly price review
review.oldest: days since the oldest price was recorded
review.provisionalTitle: These prices have not been checked
review.provisionalBody: {count} prices came from a published list of manufacturers' maximum retail prices. They are not what this clinic charges, and nobody here has reviewed them.
review.notRemindedBody: This review is open but no reminder has gone out. Tell whoever owns it.
review.noCycle: No review has been opened yet. One opens automatically on the due day each month.

import.title: Upload a price list
import.explain: A CSV file. Every line is checked on its own: a bad line is refused and named, and the good lines still go in.
import.columns: generic, trade_name, strength, form, manufacturer, unit_price_bdt, unit
import.confirm: These are the prices this clinic charges
import.confirmHelp: Leave this off for a supplier's list you have not confirmed yet.
import.refused: The file could not be read
import.summaryDry: {file}: {accepted} of {total} lines would import, {rejected} would be refused. Nothing has changed yet.
import.partialDry: The other {count} lines are fine and will import when you apply this file.
import.partialApplied: The other {count} lines went in. You do not need to upload them again.

search.title: Find a medicine
search.lede: Two letters. Trade name or generic, in English or in Bangla.
search.placeholder: Type two letters — Comet, মেট, metf…
search.rankingIncomplete: Ordered alphabetically — your own prescribing history is not in this ranking yet
search.keys: ↓ ↑ between medicines · ← → between strengths · Enter to choose · Esc to close

medicationRules.lede: The rules that check every prescription. You write them; nothing here does anything until you approve it.
medicationRules.unapprovedBanner: {count} rules were drafted from published guidance and are waiting for you. None of them is doing anything yet.

list.name: Rule
list.emptyBody: Change the filter, or write the first one.

medicationRules.unapprovedNotice: Nobody at this clinic has approved this rule. It does nothing to any prescription until you do.

preview.title: What this rule will do
preview.invalid: Not yet something that can be checked

form.codeHelp: Short, uppercase, and never reused — findings quote it.
form.sourceHelp: A guideline, a label, a paper. A rule with nothing behind it cannot be argued with.
form.subject: Which medicine
form.when: When all of this is true
form.currentMeds: Count medicines the patient is already taking

sandbox.title: Try it on a test patient
sandbox.lede: Nothing here touches a real patient. Describe one, and see exactly what this rule would do.
sandbox.notLive: This rule is not live. Nothing you see here is happening to any prescription.
sandbox.isLive: This rule is live — this is what happens now.

outcome.NOT_APPLICABLE: It does not apply to this prescription

publish.title: Publish
publish.lede: Publishing puts your name on this rule and makes it check every prescription from that moment.
publish.confirmBody: It takes effect for every physician immediately. This version is frozen forever — changing it later means drafting another. Whatever is live now is retired.
publish.blockedUnsaved: Save your changes first — publishing sends what the server holds, not what is on this screen.

withdraw.title: Withdraw
withdraw.body: It stops checking prescriptions. Every version stays, so a check run while it was live can still be reproduced.

allergens.title: Allergens and cross-reactivity
allergens.lede: What a reported allergy covers, and what it implies about something else. Drafted from the literature and waiting for you.

io.title: Import and export
io.exportHelp: Every rule, in both languages, as a file you can read away from this screen.
io.importHelp: Everything imported arrives as an unapproved draft, whatever the file says.
io.dryRun: Check the file without changing anything

renal.label: Kidney function
renal.unavailable: This patient’s kidney function could not be read. Do not read that as normal kidney function.
renal.stageIsNotADiagnosis: This is a GFR category from one result, not a diagnosis of chronic kidney disease.
renal.provisional: The {months}-month window is a proposal. No physician has approved it yet.
